principles: A chain should record the transmission claim its entry makes. I correct it when the stored links misread that claim, or when they label it differently from how hadith-kg labels the identical claim elsewhere. hadith-kg applies inqita per teacher-student pair, but book by book (al-Hasan's known breaks are fully marked in Musnad Ahmad and 'Abd al-Razzaq and never in Shu'ab or Sharh al-Sunna). An unmarked instance of a pair the source marks elsewhere is therefore a coverage gap, and I fill it so that identical text gets an identical label. I do not add gaps on chronology alone where the source has no convention for the pair, because the source leaves about 98% of t2-to-t7 links unmarked and narrator dates already carry that signal. I restore a dropped narrator only when the entry's own wording, or the same route through the same intermediaries, fixes who he is, so that a copying slip does not appear in the bundle as a dive. I never insert a narrator by conjecture.

decisions.reasoning: Ma'rifat al-Sunan 4442 (hadith 145632) reads 'عَنْ يُونُسَ بْنِ عُبَيْدٍ , عَنِ الْحَسَنِ , عَنْ عُبَادَةَ بْنِ الصَّامِتِ'. The same entry gives al-Shafi'i's second route 'عَنِالْحَسَنِ , عَنْ حِطَّانَ الرَّقَاشِيِّ ... عَنْ عُبَادَةَ' and his doubt 'وَلا أَدْرِي أَدْخَلَهُ عَبْدُ الْوَهَّابِ بَيْنَهُمَا', so the entry itself documents a missing link. The identical al-Shafi'i < 'Abd al-Wahhab < Yunus < al-Hasan < 'Ubada route is inqita in 198333, 340125, 383381, 431847. Book 24 marks 2 of its 6 al-Hasan known-break links. Pair-level data: in this tradition 'Ubada > al-Hasan carries inqita in 9 chains (75751, 189810, 198333, 307876, 340125, 355175, 383381, 426856, 431847) and none in 7 (the 7 proposals); corpus-wide 16 inqita vs 12 direct. The text form does not explain the split: the inqita chains read the same 'عن الحسن عن عبادة' (e.g. 340125 'عَنِ الْحَسَنِ ، عَنْ عُبَادَةَ بْنِ الصَّامِتِ'). The split follows book annotation coverage: for al-Hasan's critic-known breaks (Abu Hurayra, 'Ali, 'Umar, Ubayy, 'Ubada) Musnad Ahmad is 73/73 marked, Abu Ya'la 20/20, 'Abd al-Razzaq 13/13, while Shu'ab 0/22, Hilya 0/16, Tarikh Baghdad 0/13. An unmarked instance is a coverage gap, not a different reading. Bundle effect: upper_paths currently splits one asserted path into ['prophet','n:4153','g:inqita'] (9) and ['prophet','n:4153'] (7); accepting merges them. The Hittan path stays distinct, so al-Hasan's isnad variants are preserved. CL (n:1239), branch counts and dives are unchanged. al-Istidhkar 879 (hadith 425692) reads 'عَنْ قَتَادَةَ ، عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ حِطَّانَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ الرَّقَاشِيُّ'. hadith-kg mapped the whole span (mention 9, offsets 326-383) to Hittan (2415) and discarded 'الحسن'; no narrator 'al-Hasan b. Hittan' exists in rawis. So the stored chain already departs from the text, and restoring al-Hasan is the reading that accounts for every word, with 'بن' as a slip for 'عن'. The same author's al-Tamhid 1432 (418334) gives the identical route ('Abd al-Warith < Qasim < Bakr b. Hammad < Musaddad < Yahya < Ibn Abi 'Aruba < Qatada) as 'عَنْ قَتَادَةَ ، عَنِ الْحَسَنِ ، عَنْ حِطَّانَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ', stored as chain 415223 with exactly the proposed links. Of 72 Qatada chains in the tradition, 69 run Qatada < al-Hasan; the other exception (43727, Ibn Majah) names Yunus b. Jubayr in its text. Bundle effect: removes a spurious dive (currently departs n:2415, rejoins n:6458), which would otherwise count as evidence of a route bypassing the CL.

Same entry and same corrupted span as 423855 ('عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ حِطَّانَ'); this is the Ahmad b. Zuhayr < Zuhayr b. Harb < Yahya route. The proposed links equal al-Tamhid 1432's chain 415222 for the identical route. Removes the second spurious dive (departs n:2415, rejoins n:6458).

Tarikh Dimashq 52057 (hadith 627864): 'قَالَ : وَحَدَّثَنِي أَبِي ، حَدَّثَنَا وَكِيعٌ ، حَدَّثَنَا الْفَضْلُ بْنُ دَلْهَمٍ ، عَنْ قَبِيصَةَ بْنِ حُرَيْثٍ', carried from 52056 (Hibat Allah < Ibn al-Mudhhib < al-Qati'i < 'Abd Allah < Ahmad). The text does not name al-Hasan, so this is a restoration from parallels. The parallels run through the same people: Ibn al-Jawzi's Tahqiq 1904 (chain 421702), from the same Hibat Allah b. al-Husayn, reads 'عَنِ الْحَسَنِ ، عَنْ قَبِيصَةَ'; Musnad Ahmad 15592 (67545) 'عَنْ الْحَسَنِ ، عَنْ قَبِيصَةَ'. Ibn 'Asakir's own biography of al-Fadl does the same two entries later: 52058 'حَدِيثَ الْفَضْلِ بْنِ دَلْهَمٍ ، عَنِ الْحَسَنِ ، عَنْ قَبِيصَةَ' and 52063 'سَمِعَ الْحَسَنَ ، عَنْ قَبِيصَةَ'. The al-Fadl < Qabisa edge occurs in no other chain of the corpus. The stored edge is a copying slip, not any transmitter's claim. Left in place, it is the only dive on the Salama side (departs n:6452, rejoins n:1549), and an ICMA model would read it as a route bypassing the CL. The added link has no mention in the text, so text-to-chain extraction training should skip this chain or use its uncorrected form. An inqita between al-Fadl and Qabisa is not an alternative: the dive would remain, and it would label a missing person whose identity the parallels establish.

Musannaf 'Abd al-Razzaq 12990 (hadith 222430): 'عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مُحَرِّرٍ ، عَنْ حِطَّانَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ الرَّقَاشِيِّ ، عَنْ عُبَادَةَ'. The chain matches the text exactly. The chronology is right: Ibn Muharrar is t7, died under al-Mansur, and Hittan is t2, d. 71. But the record is an accurate copy of a broken claim by a narrator the aqwal table calls matruk (Ibn Hibban: 'ممن يكذب ولا يعلم'). That defect belongs to the narrator, and it is the fact ICMA needs: a weak narrator's dive past the CL. hadith-kg has no convention to mark this: the pair occurs only here; corpus-wide, t2-teacher-to-t7-student links are 2400 unmarked vs 60 inqita; Musnad Ahmad leaves all 95 t2-to-t7+ links unmarked. The Musannaf's own annotators marked all 13 of al-Hasan's known breaks and Ma'mar < Ibn al-Musayyab, but did not mark this link. A gap here would be the audit's chronological judgement, written as a label the source does not use for this class of link. Bundle effect is nil: with or without the gap the chain is a dive departing n:2415 with rejoin null, and Hittan's branch counts do not change. The break remains recoverable from tabaqa and death data, and the sanad hukm 'شديد الضعف' already records the weakness. The missing person cannot be named (Qatada < al-Hasan is plausible, given his 27 Qatada chains and the Ma'mar route that follows with 'مِثْلَهُ', but that is a guess).
